newsitem.title: USA: N.J. unemployment rate drops to 5.5 pct for Feb.
newsitem.headline: N.J. unemployment rate drops to 5.5 pct for Feb.

text.p: New Jersey's unemployment rate for February fell to 5.5 percent from 5.9 percent in January, the state's Department of Labor said Friday.

The figure, the lowest unemployment rate in six years for New Jersey, compared to a national rate of 5.3 percent for last month. That's the closest the state jobless rate has been to the nationwide average since the 1989 recession, which hit New Jersey especially hard and lasted three years.
The state lost 275,000 jobs in that downturn, and has yet to fully recover.
But the latest drop in the unemployment rate is good news for Gov. Christine Whitman, who will be seeking reelection this year.
It will also ease her job of preparing a new budget in the fiscal year starting July 1, since she can anticipate less unemployment benefits paid out and more income taxes coming in.
The Labor Department attributed the second consecutive monthly decline to mild winter weather. The jobless rate was 6.3 percent in February 1996.
The number of people working in New Jersey rose by 8,300 from January to a seasonally-adjusted level of 3.69 million last month.
The nonfarm payroll figure was at its highest level since September 1989, the Labor Department said.
